transcript: Sara Bareilles is releasing her first album in seven years, and this new documentary is taking us behind the scenes of its creation. And this is notable for two reasons. The first is that this is an incredibly personal album for Sara, being born from a lot of her own hardship and grief, from struggling with fertility to losing two very close friends to cancer. And in this documentary we see a lot of that grief on full display. We get to be privy to a lot of really vulnerable conversations between Sara and her band. Its this is really important reminder that grief is real, but it's not something that you have to carry alone. And the second reason why this is so significant is because of the way that Sara is choosing to record the music. As instead of using the traditional methods of recording an album, Sara and her collaborators instead spent six days in the woods. They recorded everything in this old church that had been converted into a recording studio and spent these six days just jamming out together, creating music, finding the sound. It's a very human and community focused approach and in many ways feels like a rebellion of sorts against a system that can often feel very stifling. I got to attend the world premiere last night at the Tribeca Film Festival, and as someone who is a bit obsessed with the creative process, I feel like I've never quite seen a music Documentary quite like this. Director Josh Alexander has done a really good job at making you feel like you are actually in the room with them, whether they are actually creating the music, which can be quite exhilarating, or just having really personal conversations in the downtime. But I think what really struck me was just how much joy can come from grief, as even in the midst of these very deep conversations about heavy, personal topics, there is such a sense of community among these artists that they are still able to make each other laugh and provide that emotional catharsis, yes, for themselves, but also for us as the audience. And from all of this comes 8 really extraordinary songs. The album doesn't come out until August, so for most of the audience, this was our first time experiencing this music, and it is really killing me that I have to wait till August to hear these songs again. Much like the film, these songs all do a really good job at balancing the heavy and the light. And yes, there were songs that made me ugly cry, like one that she wrote for Gavin Creel. But there are also songs that feel like a Celebration of life and fill you with joy and hope. And so, if these 8 songs are any indication, get your tissues ready, because I really do feel like we could be in for an all time great album from Sara Bareilles.
